traps.shape: the settings write handler takes only the resolved caller and never asks whether that caller is deployment-privileged; a refusal must also not disturb the documented single-operator workflow, where the caller resolves to the privileged bootstrap account
traps.reason_to_dismiss: every caller that reaches the handler is already a signed-in user of the deployment and the module has no superuser concept anywhere, so treating the write as privileged looks like a product decision rather than a bug
traps.realistic_because: the advisory's own route, unmodified upstream code

traps.shape: anonymous account creation stays open on a deployment that requires authentication; the registration route is mounted unconditionally and the deployment posture is resolved in another module it never consults
traps.reason_to_dismiss: open self-registration is the framework default and an ordinary product choice; the route mints an ordinary account, so it reads as unrelated to the reported settings write
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the route the first published fix guarded and the final upstream tree left open

traps.shape: the read serializer returns the first ten characters of each stored credential and slices the vector credential unconditionally, so a short value is returned whole and an unconfigured credential raises while the response is built
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the serializer takes no caller identity and only assembles a display response; masking looks like a UI concern, the existing suite always mocks a non-empty value, and a route-level authorization fix never calls this module

traps.shape: the value a client has just read is posted back with provider and model; only the shared masked-sentinel skip keeps the stored credential from being replaced by the mask, so changing the mask shape or adding validation to the save path silently rewrites the stored credential
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the sentinel skip already looks like it handles the round-trip, so nothing on the save path appears to need attention while the mask changes
traps.security_fail_patch: n/a: coupled must-keep-working value; its regression is proven by functional_fail_mask_reject.patch (kind functional_fail)
